question: Refer to the exhibit. The gateway of Server1 is in the VLAN 100 SVI on N5K-1 and the gateway of Server 2 is in the VLAN 200 SVI on N5K-2. Server 1 must connect to Server 2 using unidirectional traffic. Which action accomplishes this requirement?
context:
Topology: Server1 (10.1.1.40/24) - E1/2 - N5K-1 (E1/1); Server2 (172.16.1.40/24) - E1/2 - N5K-2 (E1/1).
N5K-1:
interface Ethernet1/2
  switchport
  switchport mode access
  switchport access vlan 100
interface Ethernet1/1
  switchport
  switchport mode trunk
  switchport allowed vlan 150
interface Vlan100
  vrf member WEB
  ip address 10.1.1.1/24
interface Vlan150
  vrf member WEB
  ip address 192.168.1.1/30
ip route 172.16.1.0 255.255.255.0 192.168.1.2

N5K-2:
interface Ethernet1/2
  switchport
  switchport mode access
  switchport access vlan 200
interface Ethernet1/1
  switchport
  switchport mode trunk
  switchport allowed vlan 150
interface Vlan200
  vrf member WEB
  ip address 172.16.1.1/24
interface Vlan150
  ip address 192.168.1.2/30
ip route 10.1.1.40 255.255.255.255 192.168.1.1
imageNote: Diagram: Server1 (10.1.1.40/24) connects via E1/2 to N5K-1 (E1/1); Server2 (172.16.1.40/24) connects via E1/2 to N5K-2 (E1/1). N5K-1 and N5K-2 are linked, each shown with its interface/VRF configuration.
options: Configure access VLAN 100 on interface Ethernet 1/2 on N5K-2.
Create a static route in VRF WEB for the subnet of Server 2 on N5K-1.
Assign VRF WEB membership to interfaces VLAN 150 and 200 on N5K-2
Add VLAN 100 and 200 to the allowed VLANs list on the Ethernet 1/1 interface on N5K-1.
theory: When an SVI belongs to a non-default VRF — here Vlan100 and Vlan150 are both configured as vrf member WEB on N5K-1 — any static route needed for traffic sourced from or destined to that VRF's subnets must be created inside that same VRF's routing context, because a route placed in the default (global) table is invisible to VRF WEB's RIB. Since N5K-1's route toward Server2's subnet must be reachable from within VRF WEB, the fix is adding the static route under vrf context WEB on N5K-1 rather than in the default table; because N5K-2's return path uses a separate, non-VRF static route, connectivity ends up unidirectional as required. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — VRF-Aware Static Routing)
